A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Doc-V* study and contain complete main texts and Appendices A–H. Textual comparison and visual inspection support reliable matching of equations, figures, tables, and relocated content.

before.justification: v1 reports original Doc-V* benchmark results, ablations, efficiency measurements, robustness analyses, and case studies in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results, including the SFT and GRPO evaluations in Table 1 and supplementary analyses in Appendices G–H.

M1.justification: Section 3, Algorithm 1, and Appendices A–C retain the same thumbnail overview, retrieval/fetch/answer actions, working memory, and SFT/GRPO training procedures. Moving Figure 2 does not change the method.

E1.justification: Both versions train on MP-DocVQA and DUDE and evaluate on those datasets plus SlideVQA, LongDocURL, and MMLongBench-Doc. The document-length scenarios and appendix case studies are unchanged.

E2.justification: The comparator sets in Tables 1–2 and the baseline configurations in Appendix F are retained. DocSeeker is newly cited in related work but is not added to an evaluated comparison.

E3.justification: The benchmark splits, metrics, training sample counts and budgets, 7B backbone, adaptive retrieval budget, and eight-step interaction limit remain unchanged. Table 6's broader 'fine-tuned' wording preserves all training indicators and specifies no altered experimental procedure.

E4.justification: Sections 4.3–4.5 retain the page-selection, document-length, efficiency, retriever, cognitive-module, and action analyses. Appendix G retains both sensitivity studies, and Appendix H retains all three case studies.

E5.justification: The point-estimate and averaging practices are unchanged. v2 adds no evaluation-run or seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests; the existing training-rollout descriptions are also retained.

E6.justification: Benchmark scores, ablation values, sensitivity results, graphical trends, and case-study outcomes are unchanged after matching relocated content. For example, Table 1 retains Doc-V* GRPO's 64.5 ANLS on DUDE and 42.1 accuracy on MMLongBench-Doc.

T1.justification: The thumbnail-grid definitions, observation and memory equations, reward definitions, and SFT/GRPO objectives in Appendices A–C are unchanged. No formal assumption, derivation, or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same OCR-free agent contribution, performance and generalization claims, and emphasis on selective evidence aggregation rather than increasing input pages.

C2.justification: The explanations involving evidence consolidation, active recovery from retrieval failures, and efficiency trade-offs are retained. The limitations still concern evaluation with one backbone and only single-document scenarios.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project GitHub repository link at the end of the abstract, providing access information absent from v1. Implementation, hardware, and hyperparameter documentation otherwise remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish the repository's contents or availability.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds DocSeeker (Yan et al., 2026) to the end-to-end methods discussion and bibliography. The Wukong reference is updated to its PDF-Wukong journal form, representing retained work rather than an additional distinct citation. The overall positioning is unchanged.

P1.justification: Table 6 changes 'Trained on Dataset?' to 'Training Dataset' and 'supervised fine-tuned' to 'fine-tuned.' Together with the abstract link and bibliographic updates, these are limited editorial changes; the main narrative and section order remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 2 moves from PDF page 3 to 4, and Table 6 moves from page 17 to 18 with revised header and caption wording. Associated text and figure placement reflow, while all nine figures and eight tables are retained.

improvement.justification: The new repository locator makes resource-access information more explicit, and the DocSeeker citation modestly improves related-work coverage. These provide limited documentation and contextualization gains. The method, experimental evidence, interpretations, and limitations remain unchanged, and repository contents cannot be assessed from the PDFs.
